newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Workers clash with riot police in central Seoul.
newsitem.headline: Workers clash with riot police in central Seoul.

text.p: At least 3,000 South Korean workers and students clashed with riot police in central Seoul on Sunday as they tried to march out of Myongdong Cathedral where union leaders are holed up, witnesses said.
Riot police fired volleys of tear gas at the workers and students, sending unprepared shoppers in the area scurrying.

The witnesses said riot police blocked the way of the workers and students who wanted to march at a nearby shopping district to protest a new labour law rammed through parliament on December 26 that has enraged the country's trade unions.
They said police clubbed a number of protesters, who threw rocks and other projectiles. Many shoppers were in tears from the gas. There were no reports of any arrests.
On Saturday, about 20,000 workers calling for the resignation of President Kim Young-sam clashed with riot police in the most violent protests since strikes erupted three weeks ago.
The new labour law allows firms to lay off workers and hire temporary staff to break strikes, shattering a jobs-for-life labour tradition.
